messages:
simon: INFRA alert — we're seeing severe NCCL allreduce bandwidth drop in us-west-2 after this morning's OFED + HCA firmware push. Affects Dedicated GPU pool (p3/p4). Impact: training jobs timing out and GPUs idling :eyes:

ana: Confirming. Canary perf tests show NCCL bandwidth down from ~90GB/s to ~18GB/s between nodes that used to be fine. CPU network traffic looks normal. dmesg on one node shows sporadic mlx5 warnings.

rkumar: We rolled OFED 5.4.1 and HCA fw bumped from 16.36 -> 16.40 0330UTC per the change log. I pushed the bundle in us-west-2 zone b and c this morning.

infra-bot: Deploy: ofed-5.4.1 + fw-16.40 applied to 24 hosts in cluster-gpu-usw2 (job id: deploy-1258).

maria: Quick checks I ran: ib_read_bw between two healthy regions (us-east) shows expected ~85GB/s. us-west hosts show ib_read_bw tcp-like stalls; sample: 
```
# us-west node
ib_read_bw -d mlx5_0 -F
# result: BW averaged 18.2 GB/sec, multiple retries
```

ana: Also ran nccl-tests (allreduce) with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO. Logs show transport falling back from IB to SHM/TCP intermittently and lots of QP retries. Kernel logs: 
```
mlx5_core 0000:00:03.0: mlx5_core: QP timeout, retry exceeded
```

ops-oncall: Is this isolated to a subset of hosts or whole region? Any differences in SKU/firmware across racks?

simon: So far limited to the two racks that were on the early rollout batch (rack ids: r-7f2, r-7f3). Other racks on previous fw/OFED are fine.

rkumar: Possible culprit: mlx5 core change in kernel 6.1 + OFED 5.4.1 handling of Path MTU / PMTU updates. Also saw a note about congestion control defaults changing in the firmware notes. Will pull the exact diff.

maria: I captured ifstat/ethtool stats. There's a lot of packet reorders and increased retransmit counters on the HCA interfaces. ethtool -S shows rx_nack and rnr_retry increments.

ana: Temporary mitigation options: 1) roll back OFED/firmware on affected racks, 2) force NCCL to not use IB: export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 (will force TCP and kill perf but jobs progress), or 3) tweak mlx5 module params (e.g., disable tso/gro on the host) as short-term.

simon: We need to balance customer uptime and cost. For prod training, fallback to TCP will increase token cost and latency. I propose: - set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on batch job driver nodes for non-latency-critical jobs, - schedule immediate rollback for the two affected racks during low traffic window, - block further OFED/fw rollout until root cause found.

rkumar: I'll prepare the rollback image (ofed-5.3 + fw-16.36) and a canary plan: rollback to 2 hosts in r-7f2 tonight at 0200 UTC, run nccl-tests + ib_read_bw + hello-world training. If green, roll back remainder of the two racks.

maria: I'll run a network-level bisect: swap PSUs between hosts and run ibv_rc_pingpong to check link-level health vs firmware. Also collecting full mlx5 core traces.

ana: FYI a known vendor note: some firmware 16.40 revisions changed the QP timeout behavior when paired with kernel backports. Might need to update kernel mlx5 driver or vendor patch. Worth opening a ticket if rollback doesn't fix.

ops-oncall: Assign to rkumar and maria. Please post runbook steps and expected impact. I'll notify SRE and customers for scheduled brief maintenance.

simon: Runbook snippet for rollback (draft):
```
# on affected host
sudo systemctl stop gpu-scheduler
sudo dpkg -i ofed-5.3-package.deb
sudo fwupdmgr install fw-16.36.bin
sudo reboot
# post-reboot verify
ibstat && ibv_rc_pingpong -D mlx5_0
nccl-tests/all_reduce
```

rkumar: Will add smoke checks and a rollback cutoff. If rollback doesn't recover, next steps are vendor escalation + kernel patching.

maria: Also adding temporary alert rule: if NCCL bw < 30GB/s for >5m across >20% of dedicated nodes, page infra-oncall.

ana: For now, to keep jobs running: set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on non-critical queues, and create a dedicated schedule for the rollback canary.

simon: Thanks team. rkumar/maria to own canary. ops-oncall to coordinate customer comms and capacity planning (we may need to spin up spare nodes in other regions to handle overflow). :shipit:
